title: Formalisme algébrique des correspondances et algèbres de Poincaré-Hodge (cf conjectures standard) : notes manuscrites (s.d.), tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), lettres (1966-1967).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues Grothendieck's letter of 4.1.67 to John Coates. It gives instructions for writing up the talk on algebraic cycles that became the Bombay paper 'Standard conjectures on algebraic cycles'. The labels here are not the published ones, as the previous page and the context show:
- A_ℓ(X,ξ) is the Lefschetz-type condition: L^{n-2i} maps algebraic classes mod homological equivalence C^i isomorphically onto C^{n-i}. This is published A(X,L).
- B(X) is homological equivalence = numerical equivalence, published D(X).
- C_ℓ(X,ξ) says Λ (equivalently the Lefschetz inverse) is induced by an algebraic correspondence. This is published B(X).
- D(X) is Künneth algebraicity, published C(X).

1) Polarization independence. If the Hodge index theorem holds for X, then A(X,ξ) is equivalent to the polarization-free B(X). The argument: B gives A by Poincaré duality on numerical classes plus hard Lefschetz injectivity, and A plus index gives B. The same then holds for C.

2) Stability. C should be presented together with its stability under:
- products;
- specialization, even with change of characteristic;
- hyperplane sections and more general linear sections.

3) Proposition (X polarized of dimension n, Y a smooth hyperplane section, products and sections given the induced polarizations). The following are equivalent:
- (i) C(X).
- (ii) C(Y) and A(X×X).
- (ii bis) C(Y) and A(X×X) only in the critical degree L²: H^{2n-2}(X×X) → H^{2n+2}(X×X). This is where the class of Λ_X, resp. of L_X, lives as a correspondence.
- (iii) C(Y) and A(X×Y).
- (iii bis) C(Y) and A(X×Y) only in the critical degree H^{2n-2} → H^{2n}, since dim X×Y = 2n−1.
- (iv) C(Y), and for i ≤ n−1 the left inverse H^i(Y) → H^i(X) of the restriction φ^i (left inverse induced by Λ_X φ_*) is algebraic.
- (iv bis) C(Y), and the transposed statement: for j ≥ n+1 the right inverse H^j(X) → H^{j-2}(Y) of the Gysin map φ_{j-2} (induced by φ*Λ_X) is algebraic.

4) Corollary. Iterating along a flag of hyperplane sections X ⊃ Y ⊃ Z ⊃ …, C(X) is equivalent to:
- (v) A° for X×X, Y×Y, Z×Z, …;
- (vi), on the next page: A° for X×Y, Y×Z, ….
So the Lefschetz standard conjecture over k reduces to the Lefschetz-type condition in a single critical degree on all even-dimensional (resp. odd-dimensional) varieties.

5) Proof sketch (next page).
- (iv) is equivalent to (iv bis) by transposition.
- (iv) implies (i) by factoring H^{2n-i}(X) → H^{2n-i-2}(Y) → H^i(Y) → H^i(X), the middle arrow being a power of Λ_Y.
- (iii bis) implies (iv) via a commutation identity between L, Λ, φ_* and φ*.
- (i) implies (iii) by stability, and (iii) implies (iii bis) trivially.

Purpose: an inductive, degree-minimal reduction of the Lefschetz standard conjecture, and a clarification of its relations with conjecture A, for Coates's write-up.
errors: The labels A–D in this letter do not match the published Bombay labels: here B = hom=num (published D), C = Λ algebraic (published B), D = Künneth (published C). Anyone reading the page without this key will misread it.

The identity used for (iii bis) ⇒ (iv) (next page), (Λ_Xφ_*)L_Y + L_X(Λ_Xφ_*) = (φ_*Λ_Yφ^* + id)φ_*, mixes Λ_X and Λ_Y (the left-hand factor is plausibly Λ_Y). As written its degrees do not obviously match. Grothendieck adds an N.B. with the transposed version. It needs checking; the intended argument is presumably correct up to such slips.
The proof of the direction (ii)/(ii bis) ⇒ (i) is only referred to ('I told you already') and is not given here.
Corollary (v)/(vi) is stated with '+ …' without precise bookkeeping of which subscripts or polarizations are needed; the typescript also alternates between A_χ and A_ℓ.

ideas.what: Under the Hodge index theorem, the Lefschetz-type condition A(X,ξ) equals hom=num and is therefore independent of the polarization
Stability of the Lefschetz standard conjecture under products, hyperplane/linear sections and specialization with change of characteristic
ideas.where_published: Partly in the Bombay paper and in Kleiman's exposés; the specialization statement is unsure

ideas.what: C(X) ⇔ C(Y) + A(X×X) or A(X×Y) restricted to the critical degree
ideas.modern_name: Inductive reduction of the Lefschetz standard conjecture B(X) to middle-degree Lefschetz-type statements (A(X×X) ⇒ B(X))
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck / Kleiman (Kleiman's proof that A(X×X) implies B(X))
ideas.where_published: The A(X×X) ⇒ B(X) part is in Kleiman 1968/1994; the critical-degree and hyperplane-induction formulation is unsure

ideas.what: C(X) ⇔ C(Y) + algebraicity of the left inverse of restriction H^i(X)→H^i(Y), i ≤ n−1 (dually, the right inverse of Gysin)
ideas.modern_name: Algebraicity of the weak-Lefschetz retraction; Lefschetz standard conjecture via inverse of restriction
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore / Kleiman; later work on the Lefschetz standard conjecture (e.g. Charles–Markman era)

ideas.what: The Lefschetz standard conjecture for all varieties over k ⇔ condition A in critical degree for all varieties of even (resp. odd) dimension, via a flag X ⊃ Y ⊃ Z ⊃ …
ideas.modern_name: Reduction of B to A in middle degree
ideas.usually_credited_to: Kleiman (B for all ⇔ A for all)

missed.claim: Explicit hyperplane-induction equivalences reducing the Lefschetz standard conjecture to a single critical degree of the Lefschetz-type condition on X×X or X×Y, plus algebraicity of the weak-Lefschetz left inverse. The global statement (A for all ⇒ B for all) is in Kleiman's exposés. The precise degree-minimal inductive form (ii bis)/(iii bis)/(iv), and the odd-dimensional version via X×Y, are not clearly credited to Grothendieck in the literature.
missed.quote: (iii bis) C_χ(Y) et A_χ(XxY)°, où l'exposant ° signifie qu'on se borne à exprimer la condition A en dimension critique H^{(2n-1)-1} → H^{(2n-1)+1}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Gives minimal test cases for the Lefschetz standard conjecture: algebraicity of a single map in one degree on products. This is relevant to current case-by-case proofs (hyperkähler varieties, abelian varieties, positive characteristic).

missed.claim: Grothendieck states openly that in characteristic p he does not know whether A_ℓ(X,ξ) and C_ℓ(X,ξ) are independent of the polarization or of ℓ, except when the index theorem is known. He also asserts stability of C under specialization with change of characteristic, which is not proved here.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Polarization independence of A in characteristic p and specialization of B across characteristics are still not fully settled in the literature.

deep.surprise_reason: Mostly the source of material that entered the Bombay paper and Kleiman's exposés. The degree-minimal inductive equivalences and the weak-Lefschetz-inverse criterion are a somewhat finer unpublished formulation, but specialists know the underlying reductions.
transcription_corrections: The subscript read as 'χ' is Grothendieck's ℓ (as in A_ℓ, C_ℓ on the previous page and in (v)): read C_ℓ, A_ℓ, B_ℓ.
In (ii), the exponent '*' is likely a struck/overtyped '°', followed by crossed-out typing ('où l'exposant °').
The handwritten addition after 'hyperplanes' probably reads 'mais lin. g.' (i.e. general linear sections), not 'non [?] lin.[?]'.
'(induit par Λ_Xφ)' in (iv) likely means Λ_Xφ_* (the comma or subscript is garbled).
